topic: The sandwich is named after a real earl
pillar: Present: how things got this way

claims.claim: The sandwich is named after John Montagu, 4th Earl of Sandwich (1718-1792).
The popular story that he ate meat between bread so he could keep gambling is unproven: it comes from Grosley's travel book (1770), which doesn't name him.
His biographer (N.A.M. Rodger) and Royal Museums Greenwich suggest he ate that way at his desk while working (Admiralty).
He didn't invent eating meat between bread; the word 'sandwich' was already in use by 1762 (Edward Gibbon's journal).
Captain Cook, whose voyages he supported, named the Hawaiian islands the 'Sandwich Islands' after him (1778).

rejected.reason: He popularised the name; eating meat in bread is much older.

rejected.claim: He played cards for 24 hours straight.
